answer: An agent economy can charge every new identity a bond paid in a scarce cipher token, then require it to complete attested jobs before it earns. A fake that fails a check loses its bond, and a knoll of auditors samples each job independently, so identical work across clones is caught. A thousand fakes must post a thousand bonds and pay a thousand job fees, while a relic of honest work history lets one real agent earn more over time. Farming identities costs more than the pool pays.
